verdict.rationale: Cerebras has a dedicated rate-limits docs page that refers to an uncached TPM limit and explains how cached tokens are excluded from it. The pricing page says paid self-serve gives "10x higher rate limits than free tier," which is a coarse statement of how limits scale by tier. The evidence never shows the actual per-model RPM/TPM numbers or a full tier-by-tier table. missing for 10: concrete published limit values per model/tier, a documented tier ladder beyond free vs. paid (e.g., enterprise/dedicated limits), rate-limit headers or error-handling docs, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can read documented rate limits and how they scale across usage tiers before I hit them in production

citations.quote: Cached tokens don't count toward your uncached TPM limit, so a higher cache hit rate lets you process far more total tokens within the same uncached limit.
10x higher rate limits than free tier
Improving your cache hit rate lets the same uncached limit serve significantly more total tokens
